B. <u>Environmental Impact of the Proposed Action; Remedial and Protective</u>

Measures
This environmental impact assessment has been conducted by the committee in the following framework which demarcates the natural environment of the Ross Ice Shelf and its subtending waters and sediments: (1) The surface of the Ross Ice Shelf, including atmosphere and snow and firn; (2) the ice between the firn and the ice/water interface at the bottom of the Ross Ice Shelf; (3) the water beneath the shelf descending to the sediments; (4) the sediments and bedrock. Within these categories of the environment, we have attempted to consider the effects of anticipated domestic, scientific, and logistic activities connected with RISP as now proposed. It should be obvious that the only major ecosystem, if at all, will exist in the water beneath the Ross Ice Shelf.
Our assessment has been conducted in accordance with procedures established by the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) of 1969. The evaluation techniques have, in part, been based on the procedure recommended by Leopold et al. (1971). This procedure employs an "Environmental Impact Assessment Matrix" as a format for comprehensive review of possible actions associated with environmental features and the possible interactions between various components of the natural environment and man's impact upon it. We wish to emphasize that the relative simplicity, as well as unknown features, characterizing the Ross Ice Shelf environments has enabled a simplification of the matrix assessment procedure; the latter was developed for more complex environments and included 100 actions and 88 environmental characteristics, contributing a total of 8800 possible interactions.
